embeds.title: Previously reported papers (still in the 30-day window)

fields.name: Decoupling Action from Egocentric Observation for World Simulation
fields.value: JD Explore Academy; the arXiv HTML source renders affiliations as one block rather than mapped per author, so the exact author-to-institution pairing within that group is not separable from the source. **FLAG: borderline** — EgoACT is a test-time framework for "egocentric action transfer" — reproducing the semantic action from an egocentric reference video in a new visual context — that operates directly on the denoising process of a video diffusion model without extra geometric estimators.

fields.name: EmbodiedWorld-200K: Toward Embodied World Agents via Embodied-Planning Dataset and Interactive World Models
fields.value: Tencent Hunyuan — The paper introduces "Embodied World Agents" (EWAs) and instantiates them as open-world embodied navigation planning.

fields.name: ActionRoPE: action as coordinates for spatially consistent control in planar-camera game world models
fields.value: Tencent — The paper targets action control in "planar-camera" game world models (top-down/isometric games), where existing feature-based action conditioning fits poorly because it gives the model no explicit world coordinate system.

fields.name: Clean Forcing: Drift-Resistant Autoregressive Video Diffusion with a Frozen Base
fields.value: NVIDIA; footnote states one author's work was done during an NVIDIA internship and two authors are co-last authors) — Autoregressive video diffusion models generate streaming video by conditioning each chunk on previously generated (imperfect) frames, which causes compounding "drift" that degrades quality within seconds.

fields.name: Vector-Quantized World Model: Latent Feedback Motion Planning for Robot Manipulation
fields.value: NVIDIA — The paper proposes VQ-WM, a latent feedback motion planner that searches over vector-quantized latent states (using a learned world model) for short paths to a goal, while a separate continuous visual-feedback controller tracks each planned state and corrects drift.

fields.name: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
fields.value: GigaAI (flag) — The paper introduces a "Stateful Harness" that separates world-state evolution from video rendering so that identical visible actions produce outcomes consistent with hidden state and explicit rules, plus WorldState-Bench, a set of 50 counterfactual pairs sharing a first frame and action but differi

fields.name: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing
fields.value: Toyota Research Institute (flag) — The paper proposes Prior-Informed Adaptation (PIA), an offline-to-online model-based RL framework for autonomous racing that pretrains a world model on low- and high-fidelity simulated trajectories, then adapts it online with limited real interaction.

fields.name: PrismWAM: Decoupling State Representations in World Action Models
fields.value: NVIDIA — PrismWAM argues that the video latents used by World Action Models (WAMs) conflate appearance (texture, color) with physical configuration (occupancy, pose), which is a poor state representation for action.

fields.name: PhysSkin++: Real-Time and Generalizable Physics-Based Animation via Self-Supervised Neural Skinning
fields.value: Ant Group (flag) — PhysSkin++ is a physics-informed framework that learns continuous neural skinning fields from static 3D geometry to build compact deformation subspaces for real-time, generalizable physics-based animation, supporting meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians as well as rig-complementary animation.

fields.name: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
fields.value: Tencent — PVBench scores the physical plausibility of generated videos across 46 dimensions spanning seven domains, using 600 paired text-to-video/image-to-video prompt groups (30% involving embodied agents such as robot arms and humanoids).

fields.name: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
fields.value: Kuaishou — Mise-en-Video (MeV) is a framework for multi-shot video generation in which creators stage each shot in 3D before generation, combining hierarchical attention for cross-shot narrative consistency with 3D-aware layout guidance for per-shot spatial control.

fields.name: ReDT: Resolution-Decoupled Visual Geometry Transformer
fields.value: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab; footnote says work done during an internship at Huawei Canada), Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai (flag) — ReDT is a feed-forward transformer for multi-view 3D reconstruction built on the VGGT family (specifically VGGT-Ω), designed to handle high-definition inputs without the quality degradation and quadratic cost that standard-definition-trained models show at higher resolutions.

fields.name: DragonMoCap: Monocular Video-based Motion Capture for Diverse Dragon Topologies
fields.value: Tencent — DragonMoCap is a monocular video motion-capture framework for dragon-type game/film characters, whose production rigs vary widely in joint count (20–60+) and naming, breaking fixed-template regressors.

fields.name: Map2Vid: Embodied Navigation Video Generation with Human-Friendly Motion Control
fields.value: Alibaba Group — Map2Vid frames embodied-navigation video generation as turning a bird's-eye-view (BEV) map of a scene and intended route into an egocentric video, as an alternative to vague text prompts or low-level camera-trajectory controls.

fields.name: MCSplat: Multi-View Photometric and Geometric Consistent Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes
fields.value: Zaofu Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.; project leaders are drawn from this company per the paper's footnote. FLAG: borderline — MCSplat is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method for reconstructing driving scenes from sparse surround-view camera images.
